A7. VERDICT LINE: 'ok  github.com/takushi/agentic-loop-foundation/v2/internal/api 0.008s'. 50 subtests = 25 routes x 2 fault shapes, every one measured 500. The decorator is test-local, over the application.Transactor port, in two variants: (A) it returns the fault INSTEAD of running the callback; (B) it runs the callback and THEN returns the fault, which is the commit-time shape -- variant B deliberately discards whatever the callback itself returned, because the property under test is that no handler can answer 2xx while Transact returns non-nil. The injected error is a plain errors.New carrying storage-shaped text copied from V2-079's measurement: a DOUBLED Firestore parent name carrying the installation key and the collection segments plus a byte offset. NO gRPC status package is imported. Per route and per variant the test asserts: status == 500; error code == internal_error; status != 400; status is not any 2xx; message is exactly the constant "internal server error"; the body contains NONE of eight fragments of the injected text (the whole string, "InvalidArgument", "StartAfter", "projects/agentic-loop-local", "install-7f3a", "byte offset", the base64url document key, "rpc error") -- matching text here proves the text is GONE, which is the opposite of classifying by text; the body carries EXACTLY the four keys error, message, schema_version and correlation_id (asserted as len(doc) == 4 and by name); and the X-Correlation-ID header is still set. The 25 routes: POST /internal/reconcile (injected through the reconcile hook, which is how that branch reaches domainError), GET and POST /v1/requirements, GET /v1/requirements/{id}, :request-input, :answer-input, :start-framing, GET and POST /v1/controls, GET /v1/queue/summary, GET /v1/runners, GET /v1/providers, GET /v1/export, POST /v1/runner/claims:acquire, POST /v1/runner/permits:check, POST /v1/executions/result, POST /v1/executions/{id}:start, POST /v1/leases/{id}:renew, POST /v1/runner/heartbeat, POST /v1/runner/checkpoints, and the five /v1/repositories routes.
